newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT-Tired dlr/mark may test support next.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-Tired dlr/mark may test support next.

text.p: Dollar/mark, showing signs of exhaustion, may visit the downside before launching a new rally to 1.7423, the 1997 high, analysts said on Tuesday.
At 1550 EDT/1950 GMT, dollar/mark traded at 1.7310/20 versus 1.7356/61 at the open, and 1.7305/15 late on Monday.
"The dollar looks a bit exhausted close to the top," said analyst Ben Morden at I.D.E.A., referring to the dollar's narrow range-trading on Tuesday.
"We could build a topping formation in the 1.7375-1.7405 area. Dollar/mark may have to dip below 1.7260/70, a critical area, before bouncing back," Morden added.

Dollar/mark set lows in the 1.7265/75 area during the three trading days between Friday and Tuesday. This suggested the formation of a triple bottom from which to launch an attack on 1.7407, the recent high on Friday, and on 1.7423, the 39-month high set on June 6.
However, the need for such pullback will not be confirmed unless 1.7275-mark support gives way -- a development that the mark's underlying weakness may prevent, chartists cautioned.
"I look at mark/yen, because if it breaks below 65.00, dollar/mark could stay firm, while dollar/yen might sell off more aggressively," Morden noted.
At 1550 EDT/1950 GMT, mark/yen was quoted at 65.46/49, off from a day's high at 65.52/57, while sterling/mark was quoted at 2.8380/90 vs. 2.8357/62 at the open.
Chartists said 65.25 mark/yen support was an important retracement level and, if it gives way, this should lead to a retest of the recent low at 64.66 on June 11.
"On sterling/mark, you have a bull flag pattern which means that you are going to see 2.85, a big psychological level, maybe as early as tomorrow," Morden predicted.
"More importantly, we are near the upper end of a rising channel since February that comes in at 2.8780," he added.
Sterling/mark has not been trading above the 2.85 level since August 1992 when the British pound dropped out of Europe's Exchange Rate Mechanism under speculative pressure.
"Sterling/mark at 2.8780, that's the implication of a break of 2.85," Morden also said.
Analysts agreed dollar/yen lacked momentum even more than dollar/mark.

"Dollar/yen offers the risk of a retest of 112.55, the 62-percent retracement of the move from 110.62, the low on June 11, to 115.70, the high on June 12," one chartist said. "If that goes, look for 111.80 and then 110.60."
